title: The Lion and the Mouse
author: Aesop, retelling
credit: An original, shortened retelling of The Aesop for Children (1919), public domain; adapted for young readers.

pages: A big lion was asleep in the sun. A little mouse ran over his nose.
The lion woke up and gently placed a paw beside the mouse.
"Please let me go," said the mouse. "Some day I will help you."
The lion laughed. "How can a tiny mouse help me?" But he let her go.
One day the lion was caught in a rope net. He roared and roared.
The mouse heard him. She chewed the rope with her sharp teeth.
Snip, snap! The lion was free. "Thank you, little friend," he said.

quiz.q: How did the mouse help the lion?
quiz.ev: She chewed the rope with her sharp teeth.
